chapter: Opinions on singers, promotion and originality
title: Singers in the Basie band: Pres, Billie Holiday and the singer as ornament
summary: Pres disliked most vocalists; Edison and Dance recall Billie Holiday with the band and say singers once merely sat on the bandstand.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Yeah, that was the end of it. But Pres didn't like it anyway. He didn't like singing, you know. Oh, Lord, he didn't like Earl Warren singing, he didn't like Lady Day's singing.
What about Helen? Didn't he like Helen Humes?
Yeah, well, he liked her. But not like Lady Day. He liked everybody. He liked everybody. He had his preferences.
Well, he appreciated Jimmy Rushing, didn't he?
Yeah. Well, he loved Jimmy Rushing. Oh, yeah, he loved Jimmy Rushing. Jimmy Rushing was a blues singer, you know. Blues is -- you know, that's the backbone of jazz, blues, you see.
Sure. Sure. And then -- because after Billie Holiday left, we didn't want any singer anyway, you know.
I heard her with the band.
Yeah, she sounded good. Scranton, Pennsylvania.
Well, to tell you the truth, I heard

her just before she left. You know, that was the first time I heard the band. I never really paid much attention to singing. And then when I heard her afterwards, when she was singing up-town, you know, when she was just singing with the trio, I appreciated her more. But with the band, I was more impressed by the band.
Right. Well, in those days, you know, a singer was just an ornament on the bandstand.
That's all. Make it brief, then, and sit down.
